answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, transferable token as collateral before it can submit bids, then slash that collateral when a dispute proves fraud. Creating a hundred hollow identities no longer multiplies influence for free: each must tie up real capital, and coordinated false claims risk losing it. The willow network can let honest agents challenge claims, while quartz receipts record deposits and slashes so penalties are auditable. The attacker pays both the cost of capital immobilized and the expected loss from detection.
